## 1. Overview

This report models short-horizon and lifetime hard drive failure risk using the
Backblaze hard drive dataset (2021-2022 sample), to inform third-party hard
drive insurance pricing. See `../README.md` for the full project summary,
data provenance, and assumptions.

## 2. Data & Sample

```{r data-summary}
events <- load_events()
cat(sprintf("Drives: %d | Models: %d | Failures observed: %d (%.3f%%)\n",
            nrow(events), n_distinct(events$model), sum(events$failed),
            100 * mean(events$failed)))
```

## 4. RQ1 - Short-Horizon Failure Classification

```{r rq1}
rq1 <- readRDS(file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "rq1_models.rds"))
cat(sprintf("Logistic regression AUC: %.4f\n", pROC::auc(rq1$roc_glm)))
cat(sprintf("Elastic-net logistic AUC: %.4f\n", pROC::auc(rq1$roc_glmnet)))
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "rq1_roc.png"))
```

## 8. Discussion

- **Limitations**: observational, enterprise-only population; SMART attribute
  availability varies by manufacturer; low failure prevalence; cost proxy in
  RQ4 is illustrative, not real market pricing.
- **Ethical/sustainability implications** of insurance-driven replacement incentives.
